correctness.rationale: For \(n\ge2\), partition \(S(n,m)\) into \(m^{n-2}\) two-level blocks indexed by the first \(n-2\) symbols. In any block, each nonempty row clique \(K_m\) contains at least \(r=m-k\) selected vertices. Two empty rows are impossible: the off-diagonal vertex \((p,i,j)\), \(i\ne j\), has only one neighbor outside its row, namely \((p,j,i)\), which would also be omitted. If exactly one row is empty, each of the other \(m-1\) rows needs at least \(r+1\) selected vertices because its mandatory selected transverse endpoint has an additional omitted neighbor. Thus every block contributes at least \(\min\{mr,(m-1)(r+1)\}=mr\), giving \(|D|\ge r m^{n-1}\). An explicit symmetric relation of degree \(r\) on \(m\) symbols with constant diagonal exists for every \(1\le r\le m-1\). Selecting all vertex words with related last-two symbols places exactly \(r\) selected vertices in every row. Every cross-row link preserves membership by relation symmetry or diagonal uniformity; each selected vertex therefore has exactly \(k\) omitted row neighbors and none across links. Every row has a selected vertex and is dominated. The \(n=1\) complete-graph base case follows separately. The actual standard-library verifier builds adjacency from the graph definition, checks 69 constructed profiles, and exhaustively examines 160164 candidate subsets for 36 small-parameter profiles. Finite tests corroborate but do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The targeted arXiv:2610.01584v1, first public 2026-10-01, explicitly states the complete formula as Conjecture 12 in Section 6 after establishing \(k=1\) for general \(m\), and \((m,k)=(3,2)\) for general \(n\). Those published special cases are acknowledged, not claimed as new. The present proof resolves every remaining parameter by a two-level lower-bound compensation and a uniform symmetric-regular-relation construction. Earlier arXiv:2606.22422 derives definitions and general estimates, including the synonymous \((0,k)\)-pitchfork parameter, but does not state the Sierpiński equality. published-finding corpus and literature/own-ledger comparisons did not reveal a covering published theorem. value.rationale: The motivating paper explicitly asks for the equality at all parameters as a conjecture. Proving it for every height \(n\ge1\), alphabet size \(m\ge2\), and \(1\le k\le m-1\) settles the natural exact-number question for the entire Sierpiński family, not a routine substitution. The lower-bound proof handles the genuine obstacle of a possibly empty row clique by deriving additional occupancy in each of the other \(m-1\) rows. A symmetric modular relation produces optimal sets uniformly without parity exceptions. The result does not purport to classify every optimal set or prove downstream complexity results.
